content.text:
I've submitted **index 10 (Ge 0.34 / Mn 0.66)** as the best composition. Its photocurrent of 1.5e-7 A was the highest of the three I measured, which used up the whole merit budget.

| Index | Ge fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 0.13 | 1.1e-7 A |
| **10** | **0.34** | **1.5e-7 A** |
| 20 | 0.44 | 5e-8 A |

- **Where the best value lies:** photocurrent peaks near Ge ≈ 0.3–0.35. It falls off on the manganese-rich side and drops more steeply toward the 50/50 composition. Index 10 sits close to the known Mn₂GeO₄ compound (Ge fraction 0.33).
- **Unmeasured compositions:** I never measured anything above Ge 0.44, so the germanium-rich half of the library is untested. I expected it to be inactive because germanium oxide absorbs very little of this light, but that's an assumption, not a result. Neighbours of index 10 (for example Ge 0.28 or 0.31) could also be slightly better; three measurements weren't enough to pin down the peak.
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements. The link to Mn₂GeO₄ comes only from the composition, not from a confirmed crystal structure.
